name: The Neon Museum
description: The Boneyard preserves hundreds of rescued Las Vegas signs, turning the city’s discarded neon into an outdoor museum of casino, motel, and roadside history.

name: Atomic Museum
description: Nevada’s official atomic-history museum covers the Nevada Test Site, nuclear testing, Cold War culture, and artifacts tied to the state’s unusual atomic legacy.

name: The Mob Museum
description: Housed in the former federal courthouse, this museum traces organized crime, law enforcement, Prohibition, and the mob’s long connection to Las Vegas.

name: Zak Bagans’ The Haunted Museum
description: A collection of macabre and allegedly haunted objects displayed inside a historic mansion; paranormal claims are part of the attraction’s lore rather than verified fact.

name: Pinball Hall of Fame
description: A huge playable collection of vintage pinball and arcade machines, including decades of coin-operated oddities that are preserved by a nonprofit museum.

name: Burlesque Hall of Fame
description: An unusual museum dedicated to the history, costumes, performers, and ephemera of American burlesque.

name: The Punk Rock Museum
description: A museum built around punk history, stage gear, handwritten material, clothing, flyers, and artifacts contributed by musicians and scenes from around the world.

name: Erotic Heritage Museum
description: A museum examining erotic art, sexuality, social history, and cultural taboos through rotating and permanent exhibits; adults-only policies apply.

name: Titanic: The Artifact Exhibition
description: A large Titanic exhibition at Luxor featuring recovered artifacts, recreated ship spaces, and interpretation of the 1912 disaster.

name: Old Las Vegas Mormon Fort State Historic Park
description: The remains of the 1855 adobe fort mark the first permanent non-Indigenous settlement in the Las Vegas Valley, long before the Strip existed.

name: Tom Devlin’s Monster Museum
description: A practical-effects museum packed with handmade monsters, masks, props, and creature-making displays from horror-film culture.

name: Outpost 51 Alien Museum
description: A compact alien-themed museum and roadside stop devoted to UFO imagery, Nevada extraterrestrial lore, and Area 51 culture.

name: Nevada State Railroad Museum — Boulder City
description: A working railroad museum on the historic Boulder Branch Line, with preserved equipment and seasonal excursion-train operations.

name: Hoover Dam
description: The immense Depression-era dam is one of Nevada’s defining feats of engineering, with monumental Art Deco details and a deep layer of construction history.

name: Historic Railroad Tunnel Trail
description: This trail follows the old rail grade used during Hoover Dam construction and passes through a chain of oversized railroad tunnels blasted through volcanic rock.

name: Seven Magic Mountains
description: Ugo Rondinone’s towering stacks of fluorescent boulders rise from the Mojave beside Interstate 15, creating one of Nevada’s most recognizable roadside art stops.

name: Pioneer Saloon
description: A 1913 pressed-tin saloon preserves bullet holes, mining-town artifacts, and the local story surrounding Clark Gable’s wait for news after Carole Lombard’s plane crash.

name: Goodsprings Cemetery
description: A desert cemetery tied to the old mining settlement, with weathered graves and local stories from Goodsprings’ boom-and-bust era; visit respectfully.

name: Nelson Ghost Town
description: The photogenic remains around Nelson preserve the violent mining history of Eldorado Canyon, with old structures, vehicles, mine relics, and desert ruins.

name: Techatticup Mine
description: Nevada’s oldest and richest hard-rock mine in the Eldorado Canyon district can be explored on guided tours through historic workings and mining equipment.

name: Nelson Plane Wreck
description: A crashed airplane used as a movie prop sits among the vehicles and relics at Eldorado Canyon Mine Tours, creating one of the property’s strangest photo stops.

name: St. Thomas Ghost Town
description: The foundations of a town abandoned to the rising waters of Lake Mead periodically re-emerged as reservoir levels fell, leaving streets and ruins visible in the desert.

name: Lost City Museum
description: Built near Ancestral Puebloan archaeological sites, the museum interprets the ancient communities of the Moapa Valley and preserves artifacts recovered before Lake Mead filled.

name: Atlatl Rock Petroglyphs
description: A staircase leads to a major Valley of Fire petroglyph panel that includes an image interpreted as an atlatl; the rock art is protected and must not be touched.

name: Mouse’s Tank Petroglyph Canyon
description: A short canyon trail passes one of Valley of Fire’s densest concentrations of petroglyphs before reaching a natural basin associated with Paiute outlaw lore.

name: Sloan Canyon Petroglyph Site
description: Sloan Canyon contains a major protected concentration of Indigenous rock art; use the official trail system and leave every panel untouched.

name: Little Finland
description: Delicate red sandstone fins, arches, and improbable eroded shapes make this remote Gold Butte formation look almost sculpted; rough-road conditions can limit access.

name: Falling Man Petroglyph Trail
description: A remote trail leads through a dense rock-art area known for the distinctive 'Falling Man' figure; stay on durable routes and never touch or trace petroglyphs.

name: Grapevine Canyon Petroglyphs
description: Hundreds of petroglyphs cover dark desert rock near Spirit Mountain in Avi Kwa Ame National Monument, an area of deep cultural importance to Indigenous peoples.

name: Ice Age Fossils State Park
description: Nevada’s newest state park interprets Ice Age fossils and the Tule Springs landscape where mammoths, camels, horses, and other Pleistocene animals once lived.

name: Tule Springs Fossil Beds National Monument
description: A protected desert landscape preserving one of the Southwest’s major Pleistocene fossil records, including mammoths and other Ice Age animals.

name: Double Negative
description: Michael Heizer’s monumental 1969 earthwork consists of enormous trenches cut into the Mormon Mesa, making the removed earth itself the artwork; the route is remote and rough.

name: City by Michael Heizer
description: The massive land-art complex 'City' stretches across the desert with abstract concrete and earth forms; visitation is controlled by reservation through Triple Aught Foundation.

name: RyanHenge
description: A homemade desert 'henge' assembled from upright concrete forms turns an otherwise empty roadside into an eccentric Nevada photo stop.

name: E.T. Fresh Jerky
description: A jerky shop leans completely into Extraterrestrial Highway culture with alien murals, props, photo ops, and a famously strange desert storefront.

name: Alien Research Center
description: A towering silver alien marks this Quonset-hut gift shop and UFO stop near the eastern end of Nevada’s Extraterrestrial Highway.

name: Extraterrestrial Highway Sign — Crystal Springs
description: The State Route 375 sign marks Nevada’s officially designated Extraterrestrial Highway and the start of the state’s best-known UFO road trip.

name: The Black Mailbox
description: The current roadside mailbox at Mail Box Road continues a long-running Area 51 pilgrimage tradition after earlier versions were removed or replaced.

name: Little A’Le’Inn
description: Rachel’s alien-themed motel, restaurant, and bar is filled with Area 51 memorabilia and has become the social center of the Extraterrestrial Highway.

name: Area 51 Back Gate
description: A public-road approach ends at the restricted Area 51 back-gate boundary; view only from the lawful public side and obey every sign, barrier, and instruction.

name: Area 51 Groom Lake Road Boundary
description: The Groom Lake Road approach reaches the famous restricted boundary associated with Area 51; stop before all warning signs and never cross the military boundary.

name: Area 51 Alien Center
description: A brightly themed alien travel stop near the Death Valley junction combines UFO souvenirs, oversized extraterrestrial imagery, and Highway 95 roadside kitsch.

name: Big Bovine of the Desert
description: An oversized cow figure in the Amargosa Valley is the sort of inexplicable desert roadside landmark that fits OddWay almost perfectly.

name: Coffinwood
description: A private property devoted to coffin-shaped art, structures, a cemetery, and macabre handmade objects; tours require advance arrangement and there are no walk-in visits.

name: Searchlight Museum
description: This small Clark County museum preserves Searchlight’s mining history, unusual residents, and artifacts from a desert town that once boomed around gold claims.

name: Laughlin Labyrinths
description: A collection of large hand-built stone labyrinths sits on desert hills above Laughlin, intended for walking and contemplation rather than as ancient archaeological features.

name: Walking Box Ranch
description: The former ranch of silent-film stars Rex Bell and Clara Bow survives in the Mojave; BLM currently allows exterior/perimeter viewing while the interior remains closed.

name: World-Famous Clown Motel
description: A clown-packed motel beside Tonopah’s old cemetery has become a modern Nevada oddity, combining thousands of clown figures with persistent haunted-hotel lore.

name: Old Tonopah Cemetery
description: The 1901–1911 cemetery contains miners, boomtown residents, and victims of the 1911 Belmont Mine fire; its position beside the Clown Motel adds to its eerie reputation.

name: Mizpah Hotel
description: This restored 1907 mining-era hotel is associated with the 'Lady in Red' ghost legend and preserves the elaborate atmosphere of Tonopah’s silver-boom years.

name: Tonopah Historic Mining Park
description: A preserved mining complex sprawls across the original Tonopah claims with headframes, shafts, machinery, and trails through the terrain that created the town.

name: Central Nevada Museum
description: A regional museum packed with mining, railroad, military, ranching, and pioneer material, including outdoor historic structures and heavy equipment.

name: Lunar Crater
description: A mile-wide volcanic maar sits along a rough BLM backcountry byway in a landscape once used for astronaut and planetary-field training; the pin is at the public crater viewpoint area.

name: Goldfield Historic Cemetery
description: The boomtown cemetery holds miners, pioneers, and eccentrically worded markers that reflect Goldfield’s rough early history; visit respectfully and leave all objects in place.

name: Paste Eater’s Grave
description: A famously bizarre cemetery marker identifies an unknown man whose epitaph says he died after eating library paste, one of Nevada’s classic strange-grave stories.

name: Goldfield Hotel
description: The imposing 1908 hotel is central to Goldfield ghost lore, including stories of an apparition called Elizabeth; unless an authorized event or tour is offered, view it only from public space.

name: Esmeralda County Courthouse
description: The 1907 courthouse still preserves elaborate original interiors and stands as one of the best surviving civic buildings from Goldfield’s sudden mining boom.

name: Goldfield High School
description: A monumental 1907 school building survives from Goldfield’s peak population, an outsized reminder of how quickly the desert boomtown grew and collapsed.

name: Goldfield Radio Museum
description: A small specialist collection preserves antique radios, communications equipment, and broadcast-era technology in one of Nevada’s most intact old mining towns.

name: International Car Forest of the Last Church
description: Dozens of painted cars, buses, and vans are planted nose-first or stacked across the desert as a sprawling, constantly weathering outdoor art installation.

name: Rhyolite Ghost Town
description: One of Nevada’s most substantial ghost towns preserves the skeletal remains of a once-booming Bullfrog mining city only a few miles from Death Valley.

name: Cook Bank Ruins
description: The three-story concrete shell of the Cook Bank is Rhyolite’s signature ruin and a stark reminder of how elaborate the short-lived town became.

name: Rhyolite Train Depot
description: The 1908 Las Vegas & Tonopah Railroad depot survives as one of Rhyolite’s most complete buildings; restoration work means the structure itself should be viewed from outside.

name: Tom Kelly Bottle House
description: Built in 1906 from thousands of discarded glass bottles set in mortar, this preserved miner’s house turns boomtown trash into one of Rhyolite’s strangest structures.

name: Rhyolite School Ruins
description: The concrete shell of Rhyolite’s large school shows how confidently the town built for a future that vanished only a few years later.

name: Goldwell Open Air Museum
description: An outdoor sculpture park beside Rhyolite fills the desert with surreal permanent works created by Belgian and other artists.

name: The Last Supper
description: Albert Szukalski’s ghostly plaster figures recreate Leonardo’s Last Supper in the open Mojave and became the sculpture that launched Goldwell Open Air Museum.

name: Lady Desert: The Venus of Nevada
description: Dr. Hugo Heyrman’s pixel-like cinder-block Venus rises from the Goldwell sculpture grounds as a deliberately anachronistic desert figure.

name: Gold Point Ghost Town
description: A privately preserved mining settlement retains cabins, saloons, equipment, and streets from Nevada’s boomtown era; public access depends on current owner operations and events.

name: Beatty Museum & Historical Society
description: The local museum interprets Beatty, nearby Rhyolite, railroads, mining, Indigenous history, and the hard-lived communities around the Bullfrog district.

name: Carrara Ghost Town
description: Scattered foundations and remnants mark a short-lived marble-company town that once had a railroad spur, hotel, and planned desert community.

name: Bonnie Claire Ghost Town
description: Remote mill ruins and scattered structures survive at a mining-and-railroad settlement on the edge of the Nevada desert; road conditions and private claims require care.

name: Blair Ghost Town
description: Stone and wooden remains from an early-1900s gold camp sit outside Silver Peak, including a substantial mill site and traces of a once-promoted company town.

name: Candelaria Ghost Town
description: A remote silver-mining district contains ruins, foundations, cemetery traces, and later mine disturbance; stay clear of active claims and unstable workings.

name: Marietta Ghost Town
description: An isolated former borax-and-mining settlement survives as scattered ruins in a basin now better known for wild burros and extreme remoteness.

name: Aurora Ghost Town
description: Once a major gold-and-silver camp claimed by both Nevada and California, Aurora is now a remote landscape of foundations, mine remains, and cemetery traces.

name: Hawthorne Ordnance Museum
description: A volunteer museum interprets the enormous Hawthorne Army Depot and displays ammunition, military equipment, uniforms, and local ordnance history.

name: Mineral County Museum
description: A dense county collection covers mining camps, railroads, military history, local fossils, Indigenous artifacts, and abandoned communities across Mineral County.

name: Delamar Ghost Town
description: Stone ruins remain from the infamous 'Widowmaker' gold camp, where silica-rich mine dust contributed to deadly lung disease among workers; access is remote and rough.

name: Pioche Boot Hill Cemetery
description: Boot Hill preserves graves from Pioche’s violent mining years, including markers tied to gunfights and the town’s reputation for frontier lawlessness.

name: Million Dollar Courthouse
description: This ornate 1872 courthouse became notorious for the extraordinary debt created by construction bonds, eventually costing taxpayers far more than its original price.

name: Overland Hotel & Saloon
description: A historic Pioche hotel and saloon trades heavily on local ghost stories while preserving the atmosphere of the old mining camp.

name: Thompson’s Opera House
description: An 1870s theater survives on Pioche’s main street and still hosts occasional events, making it a rare remnant of entertainment in a remote mining boomtown.

name: Historic Gem Theater
description: The small early movie house is a remarkably intact piece of Pioche’s 20th-century streetscape; restoration status can change, so exterior viewing is the reliable stop.

name: Pioche Aerial Tramway
description: Remnants of an old aerial ore tramway still cross the hills and historic district, leaving suspended buckets and cables above parts of town.

name: Lincoln County Historical Museum
description: A small museum collects mining equipment, household objects, photographs, and frontier material from Pioche and Lincoln County’s scattered ghost towns.

name: Bullionville Ghost Town & Cemetery
description: This short-lived mill town near Panaca left cemetery remains and traces of a once-important ore-processing settlement; treat graves and private parcels conservatively.

name: Bristol Wells Ghost Town
description: Stone ruins, mine traces, and charcoal-production history remain in a remote Lincoln County mining district reached by backcountry roads.

name: Elgin Schoolhouse State Historic Site
description: A preserved one-room schoolhouse stands in remote Rainbow Canyon; tours are scheduled or by arrangement rather than guaranteed daily access.

name: Caliente Railroad Depot
description: The oversized 1923 Mission Revival depot recalls the era when tiny Caliente was a major Union Pacific division point and railroad town.

name: Ward Charcoal Ovens State Historic Park
description: Six enormous beehive-shaped stone ovens once produced charcoal for White Pine County smelters and now stand intact in a remote state park.

name: Nevada Northern Railway Museum
description: A remarkably intact operating railroad complex preserves locomotives, shops, yards, and equipment from the copper-mining railway; excursion schedules vary.

name: East Ely Railroad Depot Museum
description: The 1907 depot preserves original railroad offices, records, furniture, and the administrative side of the Nevada Northern Railway story.

name: White Pine Public Museum
description: A local museum mixes mining history, pioneer objects, taxidermy, fossils, regional archaeology, and an outdoor collection of large historic artifacts.

name: McGill Drugstore Museum
description: A shuttered company-town drugstore survives as a time capsule with its counters, products, fixtures, prescriptions, and soda fountain largely intact.

name: Hotel Nevada & Gambling Hall
description: The six-story 1929 hotel was once Nevada’s tallest building and preserves an old-school gambling-hotel atmosphere with celebrity and mining-era memorabilia.

name: Hamilton Ghost Town
description: Stone walls, foundations, and mining debris scatter across the former White Pine silver capital; the townsite is remote and contains dangerous abandoned workings.

name: Treasure City Ghost Town
description: High on Treasure Hill above Hamilton, this abandoned silver town sits around 9,000 feet with sparse ruins and a rough, weather-sensitive approach.

name: Cherry Creek Ghost Town
description: A living near-ghost town contains old mining structures, cabins, and remnants from repeated gold-and-silver booms on the east side of the Schell Creek Range.

name: Osceola Ghost Town
description: Remote ruins and placer-mining traces mark a once-important gold camp below Wheeler Peak; roads are primitive and active claims should be respected.

name: Baker Archaeological Viewing Site
description: A short trail overlooks the excavated footprint of a large Fremont-period village, with interpretive signs explaining the community without exposing artifacts for collection.

name: Lehman Caves
description: An elaborate marble cave system beneath Great Basin National Park contains stalactites, shields, and rare cave formations; entry is by ranger-guided tour.

name: Garnet Hill Recreation Area
description: This BLM recreation area is unusual because visitors may search designated ground for naturally occurring garnets weathered from volcanic rock.

name: Belmont Ghost Town
description: Belmont retains an unusually large collection of stone and brick buildings from an 1860s silver boom, including saloon ruins, homes, and the old courthouse.

name: Belmont Courthouse State Historic Park
description: The monumental 1876 Nye County courthouse still stands in a near-ghost town; restoration and interior-access schedules are limited and should be checked before travel.

name: Dirty Dick’s Belmont Saloon
description: This generator-powered saloon is one of Belmont’s strangest surviving businesses; its hours are irregular, so verify current availability before making the backcountry drive.

name: Manhattan Mining Town
description: A tiny living mining settlement preserves old buildings, tailings, and relics from repeated gold booms, giving visitors a rare look at a ghost town that never completely died.

name: Tybo Ghost Town
description: Adobe and stone ruins survive from a remote silver-and-lead camp that boomed in the 1870s; backcountry roads and old mine hazards demand caution.

name: Ione Ghost Town
description: Known as the 'Town That Refused to Die,' Ione retains old buildings and mining remains after cycling through multiple boom-and-bust periods.

name: Berlin Ghost Town
description: Nevada State Parks preserves Berlin in arrested decay, with cabins, a machine shop, assay office, mill remains, and streets from the early-1900s mining camp.

name: Ichthyosaur Fossil House
description: A shelter within Berlin-Ichthyosaur State Park protects fossil remains of giant Triassic marine reptiles discovered high in Nevada’s mountains; building hours can be limited.

name: Grantsville Ghost Town
description: Scattered stone and wooden ruins mark a remote 19th-century mining camp in the Shoshone Mountains, accessible only by backcountry roads.

name: Stokes Castle
description: A three-story granite tower built in 1897 as a summer retreat resembles a ruined European castle standing alone above the Reese River Valley.

name: Hickison Petroglyph Recreation Area
description: A BLM trail system leads to prehistoric rock-art panels overlooking the Big Smoky Valley; the petroglyphs are protected and must not be touched.

name: Diana’s Punch Bowl
description: A steaming geothermal sinkhole rises as a travertine mound on private ranch land in remote central Nevada; landowner permission is required, and the unstable rim and scalding water make this strictly a look-don’t-touch site.

name: Eureka Sentinel Museum
description: The former Eureka Sentinel newspaper building preserves original printing presses, type, equipment, and mining-town exhibits in an unusually complete historic workspace.

name: Eureka Opera House
description: A restored 1880 opera house still hosts performances and events, preserving ornate frontier entertainment architecture in one of Nevada’s best-kept mining towns.

name: Ruby Hill Ghost Town
description: Foundations and mining remnants west of Eureka mark a once-busy silver-lead camp that rose around the Eureka mining district.

name: Palisade Ghost Town
description: A canyon railroad town once staged fake gunfights for passing train passengers; today only sparse ruins remain near active rail lines and private parcels.

name: Nevada State Prison
description: The closed 1862 territorial prison occupies a quarry site tied to Nevada’s earliest penal history and later executions; access is limited to authorized tours or events.

name: Nevada State Museum — Carson City
description: Housed in the former Carson City U.S. Mint, the museum combines CC-mint coinage, a recreated underground mine, fossils, archaeology, and Nevada natural history.

name: Nevada State Railroad Museum — Carson City
description: A major collection of locomotives and cars from Nevada’s railroad era includes equipment tied to the Virginia & Truckee and occasional operating demonstrations.

name: Stewart Indian School Cultural Center & Museum
description: The former federal boarding-school campus interprets the forced-assimilation system through Indigenous voices, surviving stone buildings, exhibits, and a self-guided trail.

name: Washoe Club & Haunted Museum
description: The historic saloon is famous for its crypt, spiral staircase, and long-running ghost stories; paranormal tours present reported experiences as part of Virginia City lore.

name: Mackay Mansion Museum
description: A preserved 1860s mining-era mansion filled with period furnishings and Comstock history also carries persistent apparition stories reported by visitors and staff.

name: Silver Queen Hotel
description: A historic hotel and saloon displays the enormous Silver Queen portrait made from thousands of silver dollars and is also associated with local ghost lore.

name: Gold Hill Hotel & Saloon
description: One of Nevada’s oldest hotels survives beside the Comstock mines and is associated with stories of named resident ghosts and unexplained activity.

name: Fourth Ward School Museum
description: A four-story 1876 schoolhouse preserves classrooms, exhibits, and an unusually intact example of Second Empire public architecture from the Comstock boom.

name: Piper’s Opera House
description: A succession of Piper theaters hosted performers, politics, boxing, and community events during the Comstock era; the surviving opera house still operates for events and tours.

name: Silver Terrace Cemeteries
description: A sprawling complex of fraternal, ethnic, religious, and civic cemeteries climbs the hillside above Virginia City, preserving the diversity of the Comstock population.

name: Chollar Mine
description: Guided tours descend into a preserved Comstock mine where visitors can see timbering, mining methods, and the underground conditions behind Virginia City’s silver wealth.

name: Ponderosa Saloon Mine Tour
description: A saloon contains the entrance to a real mine tunnel, creating an unusual combination of working bar and underground Comstock history; tours are scheduled.

name: The Way It Was Museum
description: An old-school local museum is packed with mining machinery, photographs, maps, household artifacts, and Comstock relics collected over generations.

name: St. Mary in the Mountains
description: Nevada’s oldest active Catholic church is a dramatic Gothic Revival landmark rebuilt after Virginia City’s 1875 fire, with a small museum and deep Comstock history.

name: Donovan Mill
description: This preserved stamp mill documents the transition from early ore processing to cyanide technology; the Comstock Foundation offers scheduled tours rather than unrestricted entry.

name: Sutro Tunnel
description: Adolph Sutro’s massive drainage tunnel was driven beneath the Comstock to ventilate and drain mines; the historic portal area is private property and access is by authorization only.

name: Fort Churchill State Historic Park
description: Rows of roofless adobe ruins preserve an 1860s U.S. Army post built during a turbulent period of westward expansion and conflict in western Nevada.

name: Buckland Station
description: The restored 1870s ranch house and stage station near Fort Churchill preserves an Overland-route stop built partly from materials salvaged from the abandoned fort.

name: Thunder Mountain Monument
description: Frank Van Zant spent years building a visionary complex of concrete, bottles, scrap metal, statues, and structures around a trailer in the desert.

name: Lovelock Cave Historic Site
description: A major Great Basin archaeological cave yielded ancient duck decoys, baskets, and other artifacts; the cave is protected, and nothing may be removed or disturbed.

name: Lover’s Lock Plaza
description: A small public plaza invites visitors to fasten padlocks to chains as a local ritual of enduring love, creating a Nevada variation on the global love-lock tradition.

name: Grimes Point Petroglyph Trail
description: A short BLM trail winds among basalt boulders covered in ancient petroglyphs beside the remains of Ice Age Lake Lahontan.

name: Hidden Cave
description: This archaeological cave was used for storage rather than habitation and preserved thousands of artifacts; interior access is limited to scheduled guided tours.

name: Pyramid Lake Paiute Tribe Museum & Visitors Center
description: The tribal museum presents Pyramid Lake Paiute history, culture, natural history, and the lake’s landscape from the perspective of the people whose homeland surrounds it.

name: National Automobile Museum
description: A vast collection of historic automobiles includes rare, eccentric, celebrity-owned, and one-off vehicles arranged through recreated street scenes.

name: Fly Geyser
description: A multicolored geothermal formation created after drilling on private Fly Ranch land can only be visited through authorized tours or programs; there is no general walk-up access.

name: Guru Road / Doobie Lane
description: DeWayne 'Doobie' Williams turned a dirt road outside Gerlach into a folk-art corridor of hand-built shrines, carved sayings, stone arrangements, and desert jokes.

name: Black Rock Desert Playa
description: The enormous dry-lake playa is a stark landscape used for land-speed records and Burning Man; surface conditions can become dangerous or impassable when wet.

name: Historic Jarbidge Jail
description: A tiny historic jail survives in one of Nevada’s most isolated mountain towns, recalling the rough mining camp and the region’s early law-enforcement history.

name: Metropolis Ghost Town
description: A grand school arch and hotel foundations remain from an ambitious planned farming city that failed after water problems, pests, and economic collapse.

name: Jarbidge Cemetery
description: A small mountain cemetery preserves graves from the remote mining settlement and surrounding wilderness community; visit quietly and respectfully.

name: Northeastern Nevada Museum
description: A regional museum combines Western history, Indigenous material, mining exhibits, art, and extensive wildlife displays from northeastern Nevada and beyond.

name: Western Folklife Center
description: The home of the National Cowboy Poetry Gathering preserves and presents ranching traditions, music, poetry, gear-making, and contemporary folklore of the American West.
